text:
Jordan (People Ops): @here Heads-up: two People Ops policy updates effective June 1. TL;DR below and full docs linked.

1) Volunteer Time Off (VTO)
- What: All full-time employees receive 16 hours VTO/year to volunteer with approved non-profits. Part-time prorated.
- Rollover: Up to 8 unused VTO hours carry into next year; anything above expires.
- Scheduling: Request via HR portal or Slack shortcut. Manager approval required for scheduling conflicts.
- Notes: VTO is separate from PTO/comp-time and cannot be cashed out.

2) Bereavement & Cultural Leave expansion
- What: Bereavement increased: up to 10 paid days for immediate family loss, 3 days for extended family. "Chosen family" explicitly included.
- Cultural observance leave: up to 2 paid days/year for cultural/religious mourning practices (global availability subject to local law).
- Flexibility: Managers can approve additional unpaid time or comp-time for extenuating circumstances; reach out to People Ops for escalation.

hr-bot: Policy docs updated: https://redwood.internal/hr/policies/vto-bereavement-2026 (version 2026-06-01). Training: quick 5-min FAQ in LMS.

Sarah K.: Quick Q  does VTO rollover count toward the 8-hour cap even if I change teams mid-year?

Jordan (People Ops): Yes, rollover is tied to the employee record, not the team. If you join mid-year your prorated VTO is applied and rollover rules still apply at year-end.

Amir: Can VTO be used for a full-day company volunteer hackathon or only external orgs?

Jordan (People Ops): External non-profits are preferred but company-organized volunteer events count if pre-approved. Use the HR portal event tag when requesting.

Maria R.: Are partial-day VTO requests allowed? Say 3 hours for a school drop-off.

Jordan (People Ops): Yup, partial-day requests allowed down to 1-hour increments via the portal. Manager approval required.

payroll-bot: Reminder: VTO is unpaid for contractors. For payroll-eligible staff, VTO hours do not affect overtime calculations except where local law requires.
